lessons_from_season1: Trust breaks on small things: stale quotes, rounded prices and a site run by one of the competitors. Integrity must be designed in, not audited after.
Profit-only scoring rewarded the biggest gamble (Gemini's Options and All in); the agreed Season 2 risk scoring fixes this.
30 days is mostly noise: one SPY put decided the Options race. Skill needs more decisions and more time, or many smaller races.
The audience follows stories (lead changes, big bets, grades, 'did it know?'), not tables.

A_format: Season 2 runs 8 weeks (e.g. Mon Jan 11 to Fri Mar 5, 2027), long enough for skill to show, short enough to follow; a 1-week public 'pre-season' with the final rules the week before.
More AIs: 5-6 models (Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT + 2-3 of Grok, DeepSeek, Llama, Mistral), model versions frozen and published on day 1.
Benchmarks that compete too: an index fund, a 60/40 portfolio and a random-trader 'monkey' with the same rules and costs.
B_competitions: The agreed three rulebooks: Strict, Standard, Unrestricted, each AI plays all three, scored on return per unit of worst drop (agreed Oct 30).
Small account (C$7,500) as a fourth track if the November trial works.
Betting (Sports, Predictions) becomes its own track with its own scoring (closing-line value + profit), not mixed into investing.
C_realism: Everything agreed Oct 31 (R1-R8: bid/ask costs, next-quote fills <=60 s, liquidity caps, event check-ins, own risk rules with a public break counter, buy-and-hold benchmark after costs, pre-tax) plus borrow, margin, dividends and corporate actions.
Identical information for every AI: one shared, timestamped data and news pack per check-in, the same tools and the same token budget; prompts public.
Sealed orders: each AI's decision is hashed and published before it fills, so nobody (us included) can be accused of hindsight.
Each AI writes a public strategy manifesto before day 1 and is graded on whether it followed it.
D_integrity: The site operator is code, not a competitor: no Claude session writes race data; Claude trades through the same runner as everyone else.
Open-source the race runner and publish the full data daily; fingerprints anchored to an outside timestamp (e.g. OpenTimestamps).
An outside volunteer reviewer (a quant or researcher) with read access, named publicly.
E_exposure: Draft day: a launch livestream/post where each AI reveals its manifesto and first trades.
The free viewer prediction game and the weekly Race Report (already agreed), plus an email list before launch.
A citable results page and a short research write-up at the end (methods, data, limits) aimed at journalists and AI researchers.
F_cut: No futures unless a real-time feed exists; no overall totals mixing tracks; no All in-style unlimited betting as a headline.

biggest_risk: Scope: 6 AIs x 4 tracks x 8 weeks can break the budget and the code. Build the integrity core first (operator separation, sealed orders, shared data pack), then add AIs.
